links.outcome: Hallucination detection and flagging of generated medical answers under false-positive-rate caps
links.effect: EDR@5 up to 0.390 (PubMedQA) and 0.352 (MedHallu) at strict cap γ≤0.10, rising to 0.587 with 29%-59% hallucination reduction at monitoring cap γ≤0.20.
links.quote: The trigger fires roughly 10-35 tokens before error onset, whereas a post-hoc check has zero lead time by construction.

links.outcome: Automated real-time hidden-state probe detecting erroneous LLM outputs without human review, with latency
links.effect: Probe gives viable detection across all backbone-dataset combinations, 29%-59% hallucination reduction at γ≤0.20, ~10ms latency per answer versus ~10s for multi-sample baselines.
links.quote: Probe latency is ∼10ms per answer versus ∼10s for multi-sample baselines.

unlisted_practices: Token-level calibrated hidden-state probing with a false-positive-rate-constrained operating point for streaming hallucination intervention

screen.practice: real-time hallucination detection with FPR-constrained trigger calibration
screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an explicit real-time hallucination detection and intervention guardrail (hidden-state probe with FPR-constrained calibration) designed to safeguard medical LLM outputs during streaming generation across biomedical QA benchmarks.

primary.practice: real-time hallucination detection and intervention guardrails
